The root MIT license applies to AllowIt-authored code. Third-party dependencies retain their own licenses; dependency source is obtained through the pinned Cargo, npm and Lake manifests and lockfiles.

`verification/refinement/lean/AllowitKernel.lean` is generated from the retained AllowIt kernel by [Aeneas at 557eff83ecef5083b98a52a94ca7fae63d6c1dab](https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas/tree/557eff83ecef5083b98a52a94ca7fae63d6c1dab). Its generator attribution and source references are preserved. Any Aeneas-derived portions remain under Apache-2.0; the upstream license is retained in [licenses/Aeneas-Apache-2.0.txt](licenses/Aeneas-Apache-2.0.txt). The Aeneas backend and its Mathlib dependencies are imported through the pinned Lake manifest, not relicensed here. [Charon at c8f15d7d658c86a95658f71ad99cddd4be002e04](https://github.com/AeneasVerif/charon/tree/c8f15d7d658c86a95658f71ad99cddd4be002e04), also Apache-2.0, produces the retained LLBC extraction.

The manifests under `verification/` are frozen proof inputs rather than published crates. Their bytes and original provenance remain unchanged so existing source locks and verification receipts remain reproducible; the root MIT grant covers the AllowIt-authored inputs.


## Binary distributions

The license materials in this file, the root [MIT license](LICENSE) and [licenses/](licenses/) accompany AllowIt's SDK Wasm and Solana/Soroban contract binaries. Preserve these materials when redistributing a binary. These materials also accompany binaries from historical GitHub Actions artifacts named `allowit-sdk-wasm`, `solana-sbf-evidence` and `soroban-and-native-evidence`. Older archives lack license materials and are not complete redistribution packages. Redistribute their binaries only together with the full license materials.

[licenses/dependencies/catalog.json](licenses/dependencies/catalog.json) identifies exact published crate versions and archive checksums, full license/copyright/NOTICE texts and their primary sources. It conservatively includes all registry dependencies from retained lockfile history, including build, test and target-only packages. Inclusion does not mean that every dependency is linked into every binary. Rust's standard-library notices, compiler-builtins/libm grants and complete MIT/Apache licenses are included for Rust 1.98.0 and the Solana build's Anza platform-tools v1.57 (Rust 1.95.0 fork at `ae660768afd467d131776918a1627e18920b230c`). Third-party grants are preserved separately from AllowIt's MIT grant.

Published crates that declare Apache-2.0 but omit a license file are accompanied by the complete standard Apache-2.0 text. For dual-licensed entries using this fallback, the catalog records the Apache-2.0 alternative. The `void` 1.0.2 crate declares MIT; its publisher's subsequently added MIT copyright and permission notice is retained verbatim, with that provenance recorded. The `r-efi` packages' published `AUTHORS` files include the full MIT grant, used here as the permissive alternative.

Use Python 3.11 or later. Run `python3 scripts/package-licenses.py` to verify every current locked registry dependency and license-text hash. Run `python3 scripts/package-licenses.py <artifact-directory>` to add the full companion materials to a binary archive before distribution. New dependencies or changed locked archive checksums require an updated catalog before packaging.

The native PaySH quote path pins `orca_whirlpools_core` 1.0.4 and `orca_whirlpools_macros` 1.0.4. Both checksum-verified published manifests declare Apache-2.0 and omit a license file; the catalog retains the complete authoritative Apache-2.0 text. These fixed-fee quote releases do not support the later adaptive-fee profile.

Retained dependency history includes `orca_whirlpools_core` 2.1.1 and `orca_whirlpools_macros` 1.0.5. Their checksum-verified published archives contain the Orca License, retained verbatim in the dependency catalog. These packages are not covered by AllowIt's MIT license or the standard Apache-2.0 fallback. The Orca License specifies authorized non-commercial uses and written-consent requirements for other uses.
